findings.quote: `src/lib/brand.ts` exporting `APP_NAME = 'Anacast'` and `APP_SCHEME = 'anacast'` … `NEXT_PUBLIC_MAX_UPLOAD_MB` (default 50 …) … Always render an "Open in app" button linking to `anacast://invite/<token>` … `toActionError(err)` that maps a PostgREST/RPC error to `{key, message}` … (match `message` against the catalogue keys

In Build 2 compute `maxUploadMb` with `readMaxUploadMb(process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_MAX_UPLOAD_MB)`. findings.quote: `publicEnv()` returns `{supabaseUrl, supabasePublishableKey, appUrl, maxUploadMb}` from `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_URL`, `NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_PUBLISHABLE_KEY ?? NEXT_PUBLIC_SUPABASE_ANON_KEY` … `serverEnv()` … Missing required values throw an error naming the variable
findings.problem: Two hazards for a fresh agent: (a) Next only inlines `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` values into client bundles when they are referenced as literal `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_X` expressions — a table-driven `process.env[name]` lookup returns undefined in the browser; (b) if `serverEnv()` throws whenever ANY required server var is missing, then 2.2b's Billing tab (which only needs to know whether `STRIPE_SECRET_KEY` is set) will crash on a deployment that has not yet set `SHARE_LINK_COOKIE_SECRET`/`CRON_SECRET`.
findings.fix: Add to Build 2: 'Reference every `NEXT_PUBLIC_*` variable as a literal `process.env.NEXT_PUBLIC_…` expression (Next inlines only literals). `serverEnv()` must not throw eagerly: expose per-variable accessors (e.g. `requireServerEnv("SUPABASE_SECRET_KEY")` throws with the var name and `docs/ENV.md`; `optionalServerEnv("STRIPE_SECRET_KEY")` returns `string | undefined`), so a page that only checks the Stripe key does not fail on an unrelated missing variable.'

findings.quote: run `pnpm dlx shadcn@4.19.1 init` in `apps/web` (Tailwind 4 preset, base colour neutral, CSS variables on, components path `src/components/ui`, utils `src/lib/utils.ts` exporting `cn`), then add `button input …`
findings.problem: `shadcn init` and `shadcn add` are interactive (framework/base-colour/alias prompts, overwrite confirmations) and will hang or pick defaults in a non-TTY agent session; the component path is driven by `components.json` aliases, which the prompt does not mention. The `sonner` component also adds a `next-themes` dependency the Constraints section does not anticipate.
findings.fix: Replace with: 'From `apps/web` run `pnpm dlx shadcn@4.19.1 init -y -d -b neutral --css-variables` (creates `components.json`; set its aliases to `@/components`, `@/components/ui`, `@/lib/utils`, `@/lib`, `@/hooks` so files land under `src/`), then `pnpm dlx shadcn@4.19.1 add -y -o button input label card form dialog alert badge tabs table select checkbox switch tooltip dropdown-menu separator sheet skeleton textarea sonner`. If a prompt still appears, answer it non-interactively via flags rather than by editing generated files by hand. `sonner` pulls in `next-themes` — that dependency is allowed.' Add `next-themes` to the allowed dependency list in Constraints.

findings.quote: Add `X-Frame-Options: DENY` on a second `headers()` entry whose `source` matches everything EXCEPT `/s/:path*` and `/embed/:path*` (use a negative-lookahead regex source; … for `/embed/*` also omit `frame-ancestors 'none'`)
findings.problem: The first `headers()` entry for `/(.*)` already carries the CSP with `frame-ancestors 'none'`, which also applies to `/embed/*`; the instruction to 'omit' it for `/embed/*` conflicts with the `/(.*)` source unless the CSP entry is also split, and the exact `source` pattern is left to the agent — two agents will produce different header tables and 3.4 must build on it.
findings.fix: State the header table explicitly: entry A `source: '/((?!s/|embed/).*)'` → CSP from `buildCsp({ frameAncestors: "'none'" })` + `X-Frame-Options: DENY` + HSTS + nosniff + Referrer-Policy + Permissions-Policy; entry B `source: '/s/:path*'` → the same CSP (share pages are never framed) without `X-Frame-Options`; entry C `source: '/embed/:path*'` → CSP built with `frameAncestors: '*'` and no `X-Frame-Options`, plus `X-Robots-Tag: noindex`. Export `buildCsp(options)` from `src/lib/security/csp.ts` so 3.4 extends the options instead of the strings. Add a test that the regex of entry A does not match `/s/abc` or `/embed/yt/x` but does match `/sermons` and `/login`.

findings.quote: redirect unauthenticated requests whose path starts with `/admin` or `/o` to `/login?next=…` … `isProtectedPath(pathname)`
findings.problem: 'starts with `/o`' also matches `/other`, `/onboarding` or any future public route beginning with the letter o; the paths test does not pin the boundary, so two agents can implement different predicates.
findings.fix: Define `isProtectedPath(p)` as `p === '/admin' || p.startsWith('/admin/') || p === '/o' || p.startsWith('/o/')` and add test cases: `/o` and `/o/x/dashboard` protected; `/other`, `/onboarding`, `/administrator` not protected.

findings.quote: About 30 files, most tiny (shadcn output excluded) — kept as one L session.

Record the choice in notes.
